feature: per-subchannel ordinary Channel Health Watch gate
head: ec4ac754

api.observability: Channel.healthServing() is the aggregate state (true when any endpoint is SERVING or UNIMPLEMENTED, false when every known endpoint is rejected, null before any status or before hostname resolution); Channel.healthServingAt(index) reports one endpoint in current slot order

design.watch_transport: one dedicated Watch connection per resolved endpoint; health traffic never competes with application RPC readers
design.creation: gates start during Channel.init for pre-resolved slots and when a hostname resolver publishes its first address set
design.selection: ready(), warm(), round-robin, least-request, weighted-round-robin, ring-hash, weighted-target, priority, and hasReadyConnection all skip UNKNOWN and NOT_SERVING subchannels through one health predicate
design.wait_for_ready: waits until any endpoint becomes SERVING or the call deadline expires; fail-fast calls report ConnectionUnavailable when every known endpoint is rejected
design.unimplemented: UNIMPLEMENTED disables checking for that endpoint only and allows calls through it
design.watch_failure: a Watch transport retry returns that endpoint to UNKNOWN; healthy siblings remain selectable
design.slot_shuffle: composite-policy setup recreates gates after reordering slots so each published state stays bound to its new slot
design.resolver_scope: per-endpoint Watch Channels inherit health-disabled channel options with the resolver callback and multi-endpoint selection policy cleared because the target is already concrete
design.movable_channel: the generation counter and wake Event live in a heap-owned HealthSync so gates never borrow a field inside the movable Channel value

verification.integration_test: two real loopback registries and unary responders: a NOT_SERVING endpoint plus a SERVING endpoint select the serving one, healthServingAt reports independent states, switching the serving endpoint to NOT_SERVING makes the aggregate false and rejects a fail-fast call, and switching the first endpoint to SERVING restores a successful call
verification.hostname_test: a custom address resolver publishes one loopback address for demo.local; the resolved endpoint creates a Watch gate, reports SERVING, and rejects a subsequent fail-fast call after the registry changes to NOT_SERVING
verification.recovery_test: the earlier single-endpoint test still completes a wait_for_ready call after a background task restores SERVING on the reused connection
verification.call_shape_test: NOT_SERVING still returns ConnectionUnavailable for startStreaming and startDuplex before any business connection is opened

limitations: each resolved endpoint adds one dedicated Watch connection while health checking is enabled
a hostname refresh recreates endpoint watches, so each refreshed endpoint briefly reports UNKNOWN
a custom connector is shared with its endpoint's Watch Channel and must support concurrent use
healthServingAt indexes follow the current slot order and can change after resolver or composite-policy shuffling
